passages.t: 黃檗斷際禪師宛陵錄裴相公問師曰山中四五百人幾人得和尚法師云得者莫測其數何故道在心悟豈在言說言說只是化童蒙耳問如何是佛師云即心是佛無心是道但無生心動念有無長短彼我能所等心心本是佛佛本是心心如虛空所以云佛真法身猶若虛空不用別求有求皆苦設使恒沙劫行六度萬行得佛菩提亦非究竟何以故為屬因緣造作故因緣若盡還歸無
常所以云報化非真佛亦非說法者但識自心無我無人本來是佛問聖人無心即是佛凡夫無心莫沈空寂否師云法無凡聖亦無沈寂法本不有莫作無見法本不無莫作有見有之與無盡是情見猶如幻翳所以云見聞如幻翳知覺乃眾生祖師門中只論息機忘見所以忘機則佛道隆分別則魔軍熾問心既本來是佛還修六度萬行否師云悟在於心非關六度萬行六度萬行盡是
化門接物度生邊事設使菩提真如實際解脫法身直至十地四果聖位盡是度門非關佛心心即是佛所以一切諸度門中佛心第一但無生死煩惱等心即不用菩提等法所以道佛說一切法度我一切心我無一切心何用一切法從佛至祖並不論別事唯論一心亦云一乘所以十方諦求更無餘乘此眾無枝葉唯有諸貞實所以此意難信達摩來此土至梁魏二國秖有可大師一人
密信自心言下便會即心是佛身心俱無是名大道大道本來平等所以深信含生同一真性心性不異即性即心心不異性名之為祖所以云認得心性時可說不思議問佛度眾生否師云實無眾生如來度者我尚不可得非我何可得佛與眾生皆不可得云現有三十二相及度眾生何得言無師云凡所有相皆是虛妄若見諸相非相即見如來佛與眾生盡是汝作妄見只為不識本心
謾作見解纔作佛見便被佛障作眾生見被眾生障作凡作聖作淨作穢等見盡成其障障汝心故總成輪轉猶如獼猴放一捉一無有歇期一等是學直須無學無凡無聖無淨無垢無大無小無漏無為如是一心中方便勤莊嚴聽汝學得三乘十二分教一切見解總須捨却所以除去所有唯置一床寢疾而臥秖是不起諸見無一法可得不被法障透脫三界凡聖境域始得名為出世佛
所以云稽首如空無所依出過外道心既不異法亦不異心既無為法亦無為萬法盡由心變所以我心空故諸法空千品萬類悉皆同盡十方空界同一心體心本不異法亦不異秖為汝見解不同所以差別譬如諸天共寶器食隨其福德飯色有異十方諸佛實無少法可得名為阿耨菩提秖是一心實無異相亦無光彩亦無勝負無勝故無佛相無負故無眾生相云心既無相豈得全無
三十二相八十種好化度眾生耶師云三十二相屬相凡所有相皆是虛妄八十種好屬色若以色見我是人行邪道不能見如來問佛性與眾生性為同為別師云性無同異若約三乘教即說有佛性有眾生性遂有三乘因果即有同異若約佛乘及祖師相傳即不說如是事唯有一心非同非異非因非果所以云唯此一乘道無二亦無三除佛方便說問無邊身菩薩為什麼不見如來頂
相師云實無可見何以故無邊身菩薩便是如來不應更見秖教爾不作佛見不落佛邊不作眾生見不落眾生邊不作有見不落有邊不作無見不落無邊不作凡見不落凡邊不作聖見不落聖邊但無諸見即是無邊身若有見處即名外道外道者樂於諸見菩薩於諸見而不動如來者即諸法如義所以云彌勒亦如也眾聖賢亦如也如即無生如即無滅如即無見如即無聞如來頂即
是圓見亦無圓見故不落圓邊所以佛身無為不墮諸數權以虛空為喻圓同太虛無欠無餘等閑無事莫強辯他境辯著便成識所以云圓成沈識海流轉若飄蓬秖道我知也學得也契悟也解脫也有道理也強處即如意弱處即不如意似者箇見解有什麼用處我向汝道等閑無事莫謾用心不用求真唯須息見所以內見外見俱錯佛道魔道俱惡所以文殊暫起二見貶向二鐵圍山
文殊即實智普賢即權智權實相對治究竟亦無權實唯是一心心且不佛不眾生無有異見纔有佛見便作眾生見有見無見常見斷見便成二鐵圍山被見障故祖師直指一切眾生本心本體本來是佛不假修成不屬漸次不是明暗不是明故無明不是暗故無暗所以無無明亦無無明盡入我此宗門切須在意如此見得名之為法見法故名之為佛佛法俱無名之為僧喚作無為僧
亦名一體三寶夫求法者不著佛求不著法求不著眾求應無所求不著佛求故無佛不著法求故無法不著眾求故無僧問和尚見今說法何得言無僧亦無法師云汝若見有法可說即是以音聲求我若見有我即是處所法亦無法法即是心所以祖師云付此心法時法法何曾法無法無本心始解心心法實無一法可得名坐道場道場者秖是不起諸見悟法本空喚作空如來藏本來
無一物何處有塵埃若得此中意逍遙何所論問本來無一物無物便是否師云無亦不是菩提無是處亦無無知解問何者是佛師云汝心是佛佛即是心心佛不異故云即心是佛若離於心別更無佛云若自心是佛祖師西來如何傳授師云祖師西來唯傳心佛直指汝等心本來是佛心心不異故名為祖若直下見此意即頓超三乘一切諸位本來是佛不假修成云若如此十方諸佛
出世說於何法師云十方諸佛出世秖共說一心法所以佛密付與摩訶大迦葉此一心法體盡虛空遍法界名為諸佛理論這個法豈是汝於言句上解得他亦不是於一機一境上見得他此意唯是默契得這一門名為無為法門若欲會得但知無心忽悟即得若用心擬學取即轉遠去若無岐路心一切取捨心心如木石始有學道分云如今現有種種妄念何以言無師云妄本無體即
是汝心所起汝若識心是佛心本無妄那得起心更認於妄汝若不生心動念自然無妄所以云心生則種種法生心滅則種種法滅云今正妄念起時佛在何處師云汝今覺妄起時覺正是佛可中若無妄念佛亦無何故如此為汝起心作佛見便謂有佛可成作眾生見便謂有眾生可度起心動念總是汝見處若無一切見佛有何處所如文殊纔起佛見便貶向二鐵圍山云今正悟時佛
在何處師云問從何來覺從何起語默動靜一切聲色盡是佛事何處覓佛不可更頭上安頭嘴上加嘴但莫生異見山是山水是水僧是僧俗是俗山河大地日月星辰總不出汝心三千世界都來是汝箇自己何處有許多般心外無法滿目青山虛空世界皎皎地無絲髮許與汝作見解所以一切聲色是佛之慧目法不孤起仗境方生為物之故有其多智終日說何曾說終日聞何曾聞
所以釋迦四十九年說未甞說著一字云若如此何處是菩提師云菩提無是處佛亦不得菩提眾生亦不失菩提不可以身得不可以心求一切眾生即菩提相云如何發菩提心師云菩提無所得爾今但發無所得心決定不得一法即菩提心菩提無住處是故無有得者故云我於然燈佛所無有少法可得佛即與我授記明知一切眾生本是菩提不應更得菩提爾今聞發菩提心將謂
一箇心學取佛去唯擬作佛任爾三秖劫修亦秖得箇報化佛與爾本源真性佛有何交涉故云外求有相佛與汝不相似問本既是佛那得更無四生六道種種形貌不同師云諸佛體圓更無增減流入六道處處皆圓萬類之中個個是佛譬如一團水銀分散諸處顆顆皆圓若不分時秖是一塊此一即一切一切即一種種形貌喻如屋舍捨驢屋入人屋捨人身至天身乃至聲聞緣覺菩
薩佛屋皆是汝取捨處所以有別本源之性何得有別問諸佛如何行大慈悲為眾生說法師云佛慈悲者無緣故名大慈悲慈者不見有佛可成悲者不見有眾生可度其所說法無說無示其聽法者無聞無得譬如幻士為幻人說法這個法若為道我從善知識言下領得會也悟也這個慈悲若為汝起心動念學得他見解不是自悟本心究竟無益問何者是精進師云身心不起是名第
一牢強精進纔起心向外求者名為歌利王愛游獵去心不外遊即是忍辱仙人身心俱無即是佛道問若無心行此道得否師云無心便是行此道更說什麼得與不得且如瞥起一念便是境若無一念便是境忘心自滅無復可追尋問如何是出三界師云善惡都莫思量當處便出三界如來出世為破三有若無一切心三界亦非有如一微塵破為百分九十九分是無一分是有摩訶衍
不能勝出百分俱無摩訶衍始能勝出上堂云即心是佛上至諸佛下至蠢動含靈皆有佛性同一心體所以達摩從西天來唯傳一心法直指一切眾生本來是佛不假修行但如今識取自心見自本性更莫別求云何識自心即如今言語者正是汝心若不言語又不作用心體如虛空相似無有相貌亦無方所亦不一向是無有而不可見故祖師云真性心地藏無頭亦無尾應緣而化物
方便呼為智若不應緣之時不可言其有無正應之時亦無蹤跡既知如此如今但向無中棲泊即是行諸佛路經云應無所住而生其心一切眾生輪迴生死者意緣走作心於六道不停致使受種種苦淨名云難化之人心如猿猴故以若干種法制禦其心然後調伏所以心生種種法生心滅種種法滅故知一切諸法皆由心造乃至人天地獄六道修羅盡由心造如今但學無心頓息諸
緣莫生妄想分別無人無我無貪瞋無憎愛無勝負但除却如許多種妄想性自本來清淨即是修行菩提法佛等若不會此意縱爾廣學勤苦修行木食草衣不識自心皆名邪行盡作天魔外道水陸諸神如此修行當復何益志公云本體是自心作那得文字中求如今但識自心息却思惟妄想塵勞自然不生淨名云唯置一床寢疾而臥心不起也如今臥疾攀緣都息妄想歇滅即是菩
提如今若心裏紛紛不定任爾學到三乘四果十地諸位合殺秖向凡聖中坐諸行盡歸無常勢力皆有盡期猶如箭射於空力盡還墮却歸生死輪迴如斯修行不解佛意虛受辛苦豈非大錯志公云未逢出世明師枉服大乘法藥如今但一切時中行住坐臥但學無心亦無分別亦無依倚亦無住著終日任運騰騰如癡人相似世人盡不識爾爾亦不用教人識不識心如頑石頭都無縫
罅一切法透汝心不入兀然無著如此始有少分相應透得三界境過名為佛出世不漏心相名為無漏智不作人天業不作地獄業不起一切心諸緣盡不生即此身心是自由人不是一向不生秖是隨意而生經云菩薩有意生身是也忽若未會無心著相而作者皆屬魔業乃至作淨土佛事並皆成業乃名佛障障汝心故被因果管束去住無自由分所以菩提等法本不是有如來所說
皆是化人猶如黃葉為金權止小兒啼故實無有法名阿耨菩提如今既會此意何用區區但隨緣消舊業更莫造新殃心裏明明所以舊時見解總須捨却淨名云除去所有法華云二十年中常令除糞秖是除去心中作見解處又云蠲除戲論之糞所以如來藏本自空寂并不停留一法故經云諸佛國土亦復皆空若言佛道是修學而得如此見解全無交涉或作一機一境揚眉動目秖
對相當便道契會也得證悟禪理也忽逢一人不解便道都無所知對他若得道理心中便歡喜若被他折伏不如他便即心懷惆悵如此心意學禪有何交涉任汝會得少許道理即得個心所法禪道總沒交涉所以達摩面壁都不令人有見處故云忘機是佛道分別是魔境此性縱汝迷時亦不失悟時亦不得天真自性本無迷悟盡十方虛空界元來是我一心體縱汝動用造作豈離虛
空虛空本來無大無小無漏無為無迷無悟了了見無一物亦無人亦無佛絕纖毫的量是無依倚無䊀綴一道清流是自性無生法忍何有擬議真佛無口不解說法真聽無耳其誰聞乎珍重師一日上堂開示大眾云預前若打不徹臘月三十夜到來管取爾熱亂有般外道纔見人說做工夫他便冷笑猶有遮箇在我且問爾忽然臨命終時爾將何抵敵生死爾且思量看却有個道理那
得天生彌勒自然釋迦有一般閑神野鬼纔見人有些少病便與他人說爾只放下著及至他有病又却理會不下手忙脚亂爭柰爾肉如利刀碎割做主宰不得萬般事須是閑時辦得下忙時得用多少省力休待臨渴掘井做手脚不辦遮場狼藉如何迴避前路黑暗信采胡鑽亂撞苦哉苦哉平日只學口頭三昧說禪說道喝佛罵祖到遮裏都用不著平日只管瞞人爭知道今日自瞞了
也阿鼻地獄中決定放爾不得而今末法將沈全仗有力量兄弟家負荷續佛慧命莫令斷絕今時纔有一個半個行脚只去觀山觀景不知光陰能有幾何一息不回便是來生未知甚麼頭面嗚呼勸爾兄弟家趁色力康健時討取個分曉處不被人瞞底一段大事遮些關棙子甚是容易自是爾不肯去下死志做工夫只管道難了又難好教爾知那得樹上自生底木杓爾也須自去做箇
轉變始得若是箇丈夫漢看箇公案僧問趙州狗子還有佛性也無州云無但去二六時中看箇無字晝參夜參行住坐臥著衣吃飯處阿屎放尿處心心相顧猛著精彩守箇無字日久月深打成一片忽然心花頓發悟佛祖之機便不被天下老和尚舌頭瞞便會開大口達摩西來無風起浪世尊拈花一場敗缺到這裏說甚麼閻羅老子千聖尚不柰爾何不信道直有遮般奇特為甚如此

gloss.黃檗斷際禪師宛陵錄裴相公問師曰山中四五百人幾人得和尚法師云得者莫測其數何故道在心: The Wanling Record of Chan Master Duanji of Huangbo. Minister Pei asked the master: "There are four or five hundred people on this mountain. How many of them have got the Venerable's teaching?" The master said: "Those who have got it cannot be counted. Why? The Way lies in awakening in the mind; how could it lie in words? Words are only for teaching children." He asked: "What is the Buddha?" The master said: "The mind itself is the Buddha. No-mind is the Way. Only have no mind that stirs thoughts, no mind of being and non-being, long and short, self and other, knower and known. The mind is originally the Buddha, and the Buddha is originally the mind. The mind is like empty space. So it is said: 'The true body of the Buddha is like empty space.' Do not seek elsewhere; all seeking is suffering. Even if, for aeons as many as the sands of the Ganges, you practised the six perfections (the practices of a bodhisattva) and the ten thousand practices and gained the Buddha's awakening, it would still not be final. Why? Because it belongs to what causes and conditions make. When the causes and conditions run out, it goes back to impermanence…
gloss.常所以云報化非真佛亦非說法者但識自心無我無人本來是佛問聖人無心即是佛凡夫無心莫沈: …So it is said: 'The reward body and the transformation body (the visible forms of a Buddha) are not the true Buddha, and they are not the ones who teach the Dharma.' Only know your own mind: there is no self and no other, and you are originally the Buddha." He asked: "When a sage has no mind, that is the Buddha. When an ordinary person has no mind, does he not sink into empty stillness?" The master said: "The Dharma (the truth) has no ordinary and no sage, and no sinking into stillness. The Dharma does not exist from the start, yet do not hold the view that it is nothing. The Dharma is not nothing from the start, yet do not hold the view that it exists. Existence and nonexistence are both views of feeling, like illusions seen by diseased eyes. So it is said: 'Seeing and hearing are like illusions seen by diseased eyes; knowing and perceiving are what make living beings.' In the school of the patriarchs (the founding teachers of Zen) we speak only of stopping the working of the mind and forgetting views. So when you forget the working of the mind, the Buddha's Way flourishes; when you make distinctions, the armies of Mara (the tempter) blaze." He asked: "Since the mind is originally the Buddha, should one still practise the six perfections and the ten thousand practices?" The master said: "Awakening is in the mind; it has nothing to do with the six perfections and the ten thousand practices. The six perfections and the ten thousand practices are all…
gloss.化門接物度生邊事設使菩提真如實際解脫法身直至十地四果聖位盡是度門非關佛心心即是佛: …matters of the gate of teaching, of meeting people and carrying beings across (to liberation). Even awakening, suchness (things as they truly are), the ultimate reality, liberation and the true body, right up to the ten stages and the four fruits (the ranks of saints), are all gates for carrying beings across; they have nothing to do with the Buddha mind. The mind is the Buddha, so among all the gates for carrying beings across, the Buddha mind is first. Only have no mind of birth and death, of afflictions and the like, and then you have no use for awakening and such teachings. So it is said: 'The Buddha taught all teachings to carry all my minds across. I have no minds at all; what use are all the teachings?' From the Buddha to the patriarchs, none spoke of anything else; they spoke only of the one mind, also called the one vehicle. So if you search truly in the ten directions, there is no other vehicle. 'This assembly has no branches and leaves; it has only the true and the solid.' So this meaning is hard to believe. When Bodhidharma came to this land and reached the two kingdoms of Liang and Wei, there was only one man, Master Huike, who…
gloss.密信自心言下便會即心是佛身心俱無是名大道大道本來平等所以深信含生同一真性心性不異: …secretly trusted his own mind and at a single word understood that the mind itself is the Buddha. When body and mind are both gone, this is called the great Way. The great Way is equal from the start, so one deeply trusts that all living things share one and the same true nature. Mind and nature are not different; the nature is the mind. The mind that is not different from the nature is called a patriarch (a founding teacher of Zen). So it is said: 'When you recognise the nature of the mind, you may call it beyond thought.'" He asked: "Does the Buddha carry living beings across (to liberation)?" The master said: "'In truth there are no living beings for the Tathagata (the Buddha) to carry across.' Even a self cannot be found; how could a not-self be found? Neither the Buddha nor living beings can be found." He said: "But there are the thirty-two marks (the signs on a Buddha's body), and he does carry beings across. How can you say there are none?" The master said: "'All forms are false. If you see that forms are not forms, you see the Tathagata.' The Buddha and living beings are both false views that you make, only because you do not know your original mind and…
gloss.謾作見解纔作佛見便被佛障作眾生見被眾生障作凡作聖作淨作穢等見盡成其障障汝心故總成: …idly form opinions. As soon as you hold a view of a Buddha, the Buddha blocks you; when you hold a view of living beings, living beings block you. Views of ordinary and holy, of pure and defiled, all become blocks. Because they block your mind, they all become the wheel of rebirth, like a monkey that lets go of one thing and grabs another, with no time of rest. Since it is all learning, you must simply have no learning. No ordinary and no holy, no pure and no defiled, no great and no small, no leaking (of desire) and nothing made: in this one mind, adorn yourself diligently with skilful means. Even if you learn the three vehicles (the graded paths of Buddhist practice) and the twelve kinds of scripture, you must throw away every view and understanding. So 'he cleared away all he had, put out only one bed, and lay on it sick': this is only not raising any views. There is not one thing to gain; you are not blocked by teachings; you pass free of the three worlds and the realms of ordinary and holy. Only then may you be called a Buddha who has gone beyond the world.
gloss.所以云稽首如空無所依出過外道心既不異法亦不異心既無為法亦無為萬法盡由心變所以我心: So it is said: 'I bow to you who, like space, lean on nothing and go beyond the outsiders (followers of other paths).' Since the mind is not different, things are not different; since the mind is unmade, things are unmade. All things come from changes of the mind. So because my mind is empty, all things are empty, and the thousand kinds and the ten thousand sorts are all the same. All of empty space in the ten directions is one body of mind. The mind is not different from the start, and things are not different. Only because your views differ, there are distinctions. It is like the gods who eat together from one jewelled bowl: the color of the rice differs with the merit of each. 'The Buddhas of the ten directions in truth have not the least thing to gain, and this is called supreme awakening.' It is only the one mind. In truth it has no different forms, no light, and no winning or losing. Because there is no winning, there is no form of a Buddha; because there is no losing, there is no form of a living being." He said: "Since the mind has no form, how can there be none at all of…
gloss.三十二相八十種好化度眾生耶師云三十二相屬相凡所有相皆是虛妄八十種好屬色若以色見我: …the thirty-two marks and the eighty fine features (the signs on a Buddha's body) with which he teaches and carries beings across?" The master said: "The thirty-two marks belong to form, and 'all forms are false.' The eighty fine features belong to appearance, and 'whoever sees me by appearance walks a wrong path and cannot see the Tathagata (the Buddha).'" He asked: "Is the Buddha nature the same as the nature of living beings, or different?" The master said: "Nature is neither the same nor different. If you go by the teaching of the three vehicles (the graded paths of Buddhist practice), it says there is a Buddha nature and a nature of living beings, and so there are the causes and results of the three vehicles, and so there is same and different. If you go by the Buddha vehicle and what the patriarchs passed down, they do not speak of such things. There is only the one mind, neither the same nor different, neither cause nor result. So it is said: 'There is only this one-vehicle Way; there is no second and no third, except where the Buddha spoke as a skilful means.'" He asked: "Why does the Bodhisattva of Boundless Body not see the crown of the Tathagata's head…
gloss.相師云實無可見何以故無邊身菩薩便是如來不應更見秖教爾不作佛見不落佛邊不作眾生見不: …?" The master said: "In truth there is nothing to see. Why? The Bodhisattva of Boundless Body is the Tathagata (the Buddha) himself, so he should not see him again. This only teaches you: do not hold a view of a Buddha, and do not fall to the side of the Buddha; do not hold a view of living beings, and do not fall to the side of living beings; do not hold a view of existence, and do not fall to the side of existence; do not hold a view of nonexistence, and do not fall to the side of nonexistence; do not hold a view of the ordinary, and do not fall to the side of the ordinary; do not hold a view of the holy, and do not fall to the side of the holy. Only have no views, and that is the boundless body. Where there is a view, that is called an outsider (a follower of another path). Outsiders delight in views; a bodhisattva (one who seeks awakening for all) is not moved by views. 'Tathagata' (Thus-Come) means the thusness of all things. So it is said: 'Maitreya too is thus; all the sages and worthies too are thus.' Thusness is no birth, thusness is no death, thusness is no seeing, thusness is no hearing. The crown of the Tathagata's head is…
gloss.是圓見亦無圓見故不落圓邊所以佛身無為不墮諸數權以虛空為喻圓同太虛無欠無餘等閑無事: …the perfect view, yet there is no perfect view, so he does not fall to the side of the perfect. So the Buddha's body is unmade and does not fall into any count. Space is used for it only as a comparison: it is perfect like the great void, lacking nothing and with nothing over. Be at ease with nothing to do. Do not force arguments about other realms; once you argue, it becomes consciousness. So it is said: 'The perfect sinks into the sea of consciousness and drifts on like tumbleweed.' You only say: 'I know it, I have learned it, I have accorded with it, I am liberated, I have the principle.' Where you are strong, things go as you wish; where you are weak, they do not. What use is a view like that? I tell you: be at ease with nothing to do, and do not waste your mind. You need not seek the truth; you need only stop views. So inner views and outer views are both wrong; the Buddha's way and Mara's way (the way of the tempter) are both bad. So when Manjushri (the bodhisattva of wisdom) raised two views for a moment, he was banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains.
gloss.文殊即實智普賢即權智權實相對治究竟亦無權實唯是一心心且不佛不眾生無有異見纔有佛見: Manjushri (the bodhisattva of wisdom) is real wisdom; Samantabhadra (the bodhisattva of practice) is expedient wisdom. Expedient and real oppose and cure each other, but in the end there is neither expedient nor real; there is only the one mind. The mind is neither Buddha nor living being, and has no differing views. As soon as there is a view of a Buddha, you make a view of living beings. Views of existence and nonexistence, views of permanence and annihilation, then become the two Iron Ring Mountains. Because people are blocked by views, the patriarchs (the founding teachers of Zen) pointed directly to this: the original mind and original body of all living beings is the Buddha from the start. It is not made by practice, it does not come by stages, and it is not bright or dark. Because it is not bright, there is no brightness; because it is not dark, there is no darkness. So 'there is no ignorance (literally "no brightness"), and no end of ignorance.' You who enter this school of ours must take great care with this. To see it like this is called the Dharma (the teaching); because you see the Dharma, it is called the Buddha; when Buddha and Dharma are both gone, it is called the Sangha (the community). It is called the unmade Sangha,…
gloss.亦名一體三寶夫求法者不著佛求不著法求不著眾求應無所求不著佛求故無佛不著法求故無法: …and it is also called the Three Jewels as one body (the Buddha, the teaching and the community as one). One who seeks the Dharma (the teaching) does not seek by clinging to the Buddha, does not seek by clinging to the Dharma, and does not seek by clinging to the community; he should seek nothing. Because he does not seek by clinging to the Buddha, there is no Buddha; because he does not seek by clinging to the Dharma, there is no Dharma; because he does not seek by clinging to the community, there is no Sangha." He asked: "The Venerable is preaching the Dharma right now. How can you say there is no Sangha and no Dharma?" The master said: "If you see a Dharma that can be preached, that is 'seeking me through sound.' If you see a self, that is a location. The Dharma too is no Dharma; the Dharma is the mind. So the patriarch said: 'When this mind Dharma is handed on, how has any Dharma ever been a Dharma? With no Dharma and no original mind, you begin to understand the Dharma of mind and mind.' In truth there is not one thing to gain: this is called sitting in the place of awakening. The place of awakening is only not raising views, and awakening to the fact that things are empty from the start. This is called the empty womb of the Tathagata (the Buddha nature hidden in all beings). 'From the start…
gloss.無一物何處有塵埃若得此中意逍遙何所論問本來無一物無物便是否師云無亦不是菩提無是處: …there is not a single thing; where could dust collect?' If you get the meaning of this, what more is there to say about being free and at ease?" He asked: "'From the start there is not a single thing': then is not-a-thing right?" The master said: "Nothing is not right either. Awakening has no place where it is right, and it has no knowing or understanding of nothing." He asked: "What is the Buddha?" The master said: "Your mind is the Buddha. The Buddha is the mind. Mind and Buddha are not different, so it is said: 'The mind itself is the Buddha.' Apart from the mind there is no other Buddha." He said: "If one's own mind is the Buddha, what did the patriarch (Bodhidharma) pass on when he came from the West?" The master said: "When the patriarch came from the West, he passed on only the mind Buddha. He pointed directly to this: your mind is the Buddha from the start. Mind and mind are not different, and so he is called a patriarch. If you see this meaning at once, you leap at once beyond all the ranks of the three vehicles (the graded paths of Buddhist practice). You are the Buddha from the start; it is not made by practice." He said: "If so, the Buddhas of the ten directions…
gloss.出世說於何法師云十方諸佛出世秖共說一心法所以佛密付與摩訶大迦葉此一心法體盡虛空遍: …appear in the world and preach what Dharma (teaching)?" The master said: "When the Buddhas of the ten directions appear in the world, they all preach only the Dharma of the one mind. So the Buddha secretly handed it to the great Mahakashyapa (his chief disciple). The body of this one-mind Dharma fills all of empty space and every realm of the Dharma; it is called the principle of all the Buddhas. How could you understand this Dharma through words and phrases? Nor can you see it in a single gesture or a single situation. This meaning can only be met in silent accord. This gate is called the gate of the unmade Dharma. If you want to understand it, only know no-mind, and you will suddenly awaken and have it. If you use the mind and try to learn it, you go further away. Only when you have no mind of forked roads and no mind of taking and rejecting, when the mind is like wood or stone, do you begin to have a share in learning the Way." He said: "Right now there are all kinds of false thoughts. How can you say there are none?" The master said: "Falsehood has no substance from the start; it…
gloss.是汝心所起汝若識心是佛心本無妄那得起心更認於妄汝若不生心動念自然無妄所以云心生則: …is what your mind raises. If you know that the mind is the Buddha, the mind has no falsehood from the start. How could you raise the mind and then take up falsehood? If you do not raise the mind and move thoughts, there is naturally no falsehood. So it is said: 'When the mind arises, all kinds of things arise; when the mind ceases, all kinds of things cease.'" He said: "At the very moment when false thoughts arise, where is the Buddha?" The master said: "When you now notice that falsehood arises, that noticing itself is the Buddha. If there were no false thoughts, there would be no Buddha either. Why is this? Because you raise the mind and make a view of a Buddha, you then say there is a Buddha to become; you make a view of living beings, and you then say there are living beings to carry across (to liberation). Raising the mind and moving thoughts are all places where you hold views. If there are no views at all, where would the Buddha be? It is like Manjushri (the bodhisattva of wisdom): as soon as he raised a view of a Buddha, he was banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains." He said: "At the very moment of awakening, where is the Buddha…
gloss.在何處師云問從何來覺從何起語默動靜一切聲色盡是佛事何處覓佛不可更頭上安頭嘴上加嘴: …?" The master said: "Where does your question come from? Where does your noticing arise from? Speech and silence, movement and stillness, all sounds and sights: all are the Buddha's work. Where would you look for the Buddha? You must not put another head on top of your head or add another mouth to your mouth. Only do not raise views of difference: the mountain is the mountain, the water is the water, the monk is the monk, the layman is the layman. The mountains, the rivers and the great earth, the sun, the moon and the stars: none of them is outside your mind. The whole universe of three thousand worlds is your own self. Where are there so many kinds? Outside the mind there is nothing; green mountains fill the eyes. Empty space and the world are bright and clear, without a hair's breadth for you to make a view of. So all sounds and sights are the Buddha's eye of wisdom. Things do not arise alone; they arise by depending on circumstances. Because of beings, there is so much wisdom. Talking all day, when has one ever talked? Hearing all day, when has one ever heard?
gloss.所以釋迦四十九年說未甞說著一字云若如此何處是菩提師云菩提無是處佛亦不得菩提眾生亦: So Shakyamuni (the Buddha) preached for forty-nine years and never spoke a single word." He said: "If so, where is awakening?" The master said: "Awakening has no place. The Buddha does not gain awakening, and living beings do not lose it. It cannot be gained with the body or sought with the mind. All living beings are the form of awakening." He said: "How does one raise the mind of awakening?" The master said: "Awakening has nothing to gain. Now only raise the mind that gains nothing, and firmly gain not one thing: that is the mind of awakening. Awakening has no place to dwell, and so there is no one who gains it. So it is said: 'With the Buddha Dipankara (a Buddha of the distant past) I had not the least thing to gain, and so the Buddha foretold my Buddhahood.' Clearly all living beings are awakening from the start and should not gain awakening again. Now you hear of raising the mind of awakening, and you think…
gloss.一箇心學取佛去唯擬作佛任爾三秖劫修亦秖得箇報化佛與爾本源真性佛有何交涉故云外求有: …that you will take a mind and learn to grasp the Buddha, and you only intend to become a Buddha. Even if you practise for three countless aeons, you will only gain a reward-body or transformation-body Buddha (a Buddha in visible form). What has that to do with the Buddha of your original true nature? So it is said: 'If you seek outside for a Buddha with form, it is nothing like you.'" He asked: "Since we are the Buddha from the start, how is it that there are still the four kinds of birth and the six paths (the realms of rebirth), with all their different shapes?" The master said: "The body of all the Buddhas is whole, with nothing added or taken away. Flowing into the six paths, it is whole everywhere. Among the ten thousand kinds, each one is a Buddha. It is like a ball of quicksilver: scattered everywhere, every drop is round; when it is not divided, it is only one lump. This one is all, and all is this one. The different shapes are like houses. You leave a donkey's house and enter a man's house; you leave a man's body and reach a god's body; and so on to the houses of the hearers, the solitary Buddhas, the bodhisattvas…
gloss.薩佛屋皆是汝取捨處所以有別本源之性何得有別問諸佛如何行大慈悲為眾生說法師云佛慈悲: …and the Buddhas: all are places where you take and reject, and so there are differences. How could the original nature have differences?" He asked: "How do the Buddhas practise great kindness and compassion and preach the Dharma (the teaching) for living beings?" The master said: "The kindness and compassion of a Buddha has no object, so it is called great kindness and compassion. Kindness does not see a Buddha to become; compassion does not see living beings to carry across (to liberation). The Dharma they preach is no preaching and no showing; those who hear the Dharma have no hearing and no gaining. It is like a magician preaching to people he has conjured. How can one say of this Dharma, 'I took it in at a word from a good teacher, I understood it, I awakened'? As for this kindness and compassion, if you raise the mind and move thoughts to learn his views, and do not awaken yourself to your original mind, in the end it does no good." He asked: "What is diligence?" The master said: "When body and mind do not arise, this is called the foremost…
gloss.一牢強精進纔起心向外求者名為歌利王愛游獵去心不外遊即是忍辱仙人身心俱無即是佛道問: …firm diligence. As soon as you raise the mind and seek outside, it is called King Kali (a cruel king of legend) going off on the hunt he loves. When the mind does not roam outside, that is the hermit of patience. When body and mind are both gone, that is the Buddha's Way." He asked: "If one has no mind, can one follow this Way?" The master said: "No-mind is itself following this Way. What more is there to say about can or cannot? If a single thought flickers up, that is an object; if there is not a single thought, then objects are forgotten and the mind ceases by itself, and there is nothing left to chase." He asked: "What is it to leave the three worlds (the realms of desire, form and formlessness)?" The master said: "Do not think of good or evil at all, and right where you are you leave the three worlds. The Tathagata (the Buddha) appeared in the world to break the three kinds of existence. If there is no mind at all, the three worlds do not exist either. It is like a speck of dust broken into a hundred parts: if ninety-nine parts are nothing and one part is something, the Great Vehicle (the Mahayana)…
gloss.不能勝出百分俱無摩訶衍始能勝出上堂云即心是佛上至諸佛下至蠢動含靈皆有佛性同一心體: …cannot rise clear of it. Only when all hundred parts are nothing can the Great Vehicle (the Mahayana) rise clear." The master went up into the hall and said: "The mind itself is the Buddha. From all the Buddhas above to the crawling insects below, everything that lives has the Buddha nature and the same one body of mind. So when Bodhidharma came from India, he passed on only the Dharma (the teaching) of the one mind. He pointed directly to this: all living beings are the Buddha from the start and need no practice. Only now know your own mind and see your own original nature, and do not seek anything else. How do you know your own mind? The one speaking right now is your mind. When you do not speak and do not act, the body of the mind is like empty space. It has no shape and no place, and yet it is not simply nothing: it is there but cannot be seen. So the patriarch said: 'The true nature is the hidden ground of the mind; it has no head and no tail. It responds to conditions and transforms things,…
gloss.方便呼為智若不應緣之時不可言其有無正應之時亦無蹤跡既知如此如今但向無中棲泊即是行: …and for convenience we call it wisdom.' When it is not responding to conditions, you cannot say it exists or does not; when it is responding, it leaves no trace. Since you know this, now only rest in nothing, and that is walking the road of all the Buddhas. The sutra (scripture) says: 'Let the mind arise without dwelling anywhere.' All living beings turn in the round of birth and death because their thoughts run after things and their minds never stop moving in the six paths (the realms of rebirth), and so they suffer all kinds of pain. Vimalakirti (a wise layman of the sutras) said: 'People who are hard to teach have minds like monkeys, so many kinds of teaching are used to restrain their minds, and then they are tamed.' So when the mind arises, all kinds of things arise; when the mind ceases, all kinds of things cease. So know that all things are made by the mind: humans, gods and the hells, the six paths and the asuras (warring demigods), all are made by the mind. Now only learn no-mind, and at once stop all…
gloss.緣莫生妄想分別無人無我無貪瞋無憎愛無勝負但除却如許多種妄想性自本來清淨即是修行菩: …conditions, and do not raise false thoughts and distinctions. No other and no self, no greed and no anger, no hate and no love, no winning and no losing. Only clear away all these many kinds of false thought, and your nature is pure from the start: that is practising awakening, the Dharma (the teaching), the Buddha and the rest. If you do not understand this, then even if you learn widely, practise with toil, eat from trees and wear grass, you do not know your own mind, and it is all called wrong practice; you all become heavenly demons, outsiders (followers of other paths) and the spirits of land and water. What good is practice like this? Master Zhi (Baozhi, an early Chinese monk) said: 'The original body is made by your own mind; how could you seek it in writing?' Now only know your own mind and stop thinking, and false thoughts and worldly dust will not arise by themselves. Vimalakirti (a wise layman of the sutras) said: 'He put out only one bed and lay on it sick.' That is, the mind does not arise. Now when you lie sick, all clinging to conditions stops and false thoughts cease: that is awakening…
gloss.提如今若心裏紛紛不定任爾學到三乘四果十地諸位合殺秖向凡聖中坐諸行盡歸無常勢力皆有: …Now if your mind is in turmoil and unsettled, even if you learn your way through all the ranks of the three vehicles, the four fruits and the ten stages (the grades of Buddhist attainment), in the end you only sit among the ordinary and the holy. All actions return to impermanence; every power has its time to end. It is like an arrow shot into the sky: when its force is spent, it falls back, and you return to the wheel of birth and death. Practice like this does not understand the Buddha's meaning; you suffer hardship for nothing. Is that not a great mistake? Master Zhi said: 'If you have not met a clear teacher who has gone beyond the world, you take the medicine of the Great Vehicle in vain.' Now at all times, walking, standing, sitting and lying down, only learn no-mind, with no distinctions, nothing to lean on and nothing to dwell on. All day let things go as they go, carefree, like a fool. People will not know you at all, and you need not make them know you or not. The mind is like a hard stone with no crack…
gloss.罅一切法透汝心不入兀然無著如此始有少分相應透得三界境過名為佛出世不漏心相名為無漏: …or gap. Nothing can get into your mind; it stands alone and clings to nothing. Only like this do you begin to accord with it a little. To pass beyond the realms of the three worlds is called a Buddha appearing in the world. Not to let the mind leak out into forms is called wisdom without leaking (of desire). Make no karma (deeds that bring results) for the realms of humans and gods, make no karma for the hells, raise no mind at all, and no conditions arise: then this very body and mind is a free person. It is not that nothing ever arises; it is only that things arise as you will. As the sutra says: 'A bodhisattva has a body born of will.' If you have not yet understood no-mind and you act while clinging to forms, it is all the work of Mara (the tempter). Even doing the Buddha's work for the Pure Land (a Buddha's paradise) all becomes karma, and it is called the Buddha block. Because it blocks your mind, you are bound by cause and effect and have no freedom to go or stay. So awakening and such teachings do not exist from the start. What the Tathagata (the Buddha) taught…
gloss.皆是化人猶如黃葉為金權止小兒啼故實無有法名阿耨菩提如今既會此意何用區區但隨緣消舊: …was all to teach people, like calling yellow leaves gold to stop a child crying for a while. So in truth there is no thing called supreme awakening. Now that you understand this, why go on striving? Only use up your old karma (the results of past deeds) as conditions come, and do not make new trouble. Be clear in your mind, and so you must throw away all your old views. Vimalakirti said: 'Clear away all that you have.' The Lotus Sutra says: 'For twenty years he always had him clear away dung.' This only means clearing away the place in the mind that makes views. It also says: 'Clear away the dung of idle talk.' So the womb of the Tathagata (the Buddha nature hidden in all beings) is empty and still from the start, and keeps not a single thing. So the sutra says: 'The lands of all the Buddhas are empty too.' If you say the Buddha's Way is gained by practice and learning, a view like that has nothing to do with it. Or someone makes a gesture or sets a scene, raises an eyebrow or moves an eye, and only…
gloss.對相當便道契會也得證悟禪理也忽逢一人不解便道都無所知對他若得道理心中便歡喜若被他: …when the response matches, he says, 'I have accorded with it, I have realised the principle of Zen.' If he meets someone who does not understand, he says that person knows nothing at all. If he gets the better of the other in argument, he is glad in his heart; if the other defeats him and he is not as good, his heart fills with gloom. What has learning Zen with a mind like this to do with it? Even if you understand a little of the principle, you only gain a passing state of mind; it has nothing at all to do with the Way of Zen. So Bodhidharma faced the wall and did not let anyone have a place to stand a view. So it is said: 'Forgetting the working of the mind is the Buddha's Way; making distinctions is the realm of Mara (the tempter).' This nature is not lost when you are deluded, and not gained when you awaken. Your own nature, as it is by nature, has no delusion and no awakening from the start. All of empty space in the ten directions is from the start the body of my one mind. Even when you move and act and make things, how could you leave empty…
gloss.空虛空本來無大無小無漏無為無迷無悟了了見無一物亦無人亦無佛絕纖毫的量是無依倚無䊀: …space? Empty space from the start has no great and no small, no leaking (of desire) and nothing made, no delusion and no awakening. You see clearly that there is not one thing: no person and no Buddha. Beyond the least measure, it leans on nothing and is tied to nothing. A single clear stream: this is your own nature, the acceptance that nothing is born. What is there to deliberate? The true Buddha has no mouth and does not know how to preach the Dharma (the teaching); true hearing has no ears, so who hears? Take care." One day the master went up into the hall and taught the assembly: "If you do not break through beforehand, when the thirtieth night of the twelfth month (the last night of the year) comes, you will surely be in a hot panic. There is a kind of outsider who, as soon as he hears people speak of doing the work, laughs coldly: 'So there is still this!' Let me ask you: when the end of your life suddenly comes, what will you use to hold off birth and death? Think it over, and you will see there is a reason for it. How…
gloss.得天生彌勒自然釋迦有一般閑神野鬼纔見人有些少病便與他人說爾只放下著及至他有病又却: …could there be a Maitreya (the Buddha to come) born so by nature, or a Shakyamuni (the Buddha) who is so of himself? There is a kind of idle ghost and wild spirit who, as soon as he sees someone a little ill, tells him, 'Just let it go.' But when he falls ill himself, he cannot handle it and flails about in panic. What can he do when his flesh is cut to pieces as if by sharp knives, and he cannot be master of himself? All things must be made ready when you have leisure, so that you can use them when you are hard pressed and save much effort. Do not wait until you are thirsty to dig a well, when your hands and feet can no longer do the work. When that mess comes, how will you escape it? The road ahead is dark, and you blunder and crash about at random. What misery, what misery! Every day you learn only the samadhi (meditative absorption) of the mouth. You talk of Zen and talk of the Way, you shout at the Buddhas and curse the patriarchs, but when you get here none of it is of any use. Every day you only fool others; how would you know that today you have fooled yourself…
gloss.也阿鼻地獄中決定放爾不得而今末法將沈全仗有力量兄弟家負荷續佛慧命莫令斷絕今時纔有: …? In the Avici hell (the lowest hell) you will surely not be let off. Now the Dharma (the teaching), in its last age, is about to sink, and everything depends on brothers with the strength to carry it, to continue the wisdom life of the Buddha and not let it be cut off. Nowadays, when there are one or two pilgrims, they only go to look at mountains and scenery, not knowing how much time they have. When one breath does not come back, that is the next life, and who knows with what head and face. Alas! I urge you, brothers: while your body is strong and healthy, find a place of clear understanding. This one great matter of not being fooled by anyone: its key points are very easy. It is only that you will not make a do-or-die resolve and do the work, and you only keep saying that it is hard and hard again. I should let you know: how could a wooden ladle grow on a tree by itself? You too must go yourself and make…
gloss.轉變始得若是箇丈夫漢看箇公案僧問趙州狗子還有佛性也無州云無但去二六時中看箇無字晝: …a turn; only then will it work. If you are a real man, look at a koan (a case for meditation). A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” Just look at the word *mu* (無) through all the hours of day and night. Study it by day and study it by night, walking, standing, sitting and lying down, while dressing and eating, while shitting and pissing. Mind after mind, watch it; put all your fierce energy into it, and guard the word *mu*. As the days and months go deep, it becomes one whole piece, and suddenly the flower of the mind bursts open and you awaken to the working of the Buddhas and the patriarchs. Then you will not be fooled by the tongues of the old monks of the world, and you will be able to open your great mouth. Bodhidharma coming from the West raised waves where there was no wind; the World-Honored One (the Buddha) holding up a flower was a total failure. When you get here, why speak of old King Yama (the judge of the dead)? Even the thousand sages can do nothing with you. You do not believe that there is truly such a wonder? Why is it so?…
